summary:
Chinese Crude Sourcing Offers Continued Support to VLCCs
The rapid growth of Chinese oil product demand, refining capacity and crude imports has been a supportive feature of crude tanker demand for years, and is poised to continue this trend. Recent shifts in Chinese crude import volumes and sourcing patterns have provided a recent boost to tanker demand in 1h12 and have allowed VLCC earnings to recover. Many of these crude import shifts are part of a secular trend that will continue to be supportive for the sector, but some of the recent activity is more ephemeral, suggesting that demand growth may slow during the balance of 2012.

children.title: AG
children.summary: Africa Lat Amer FSU/Other Asia The pattern of African imports, in contrast, has been subject to the movement of the price spread between Brent and Dubai crudes, which determines the relative attractiveness of Brent price-linked grades in West Africa (WAF) to Asian refiners. As OPEC reduced the output of heavy/sour AG grades during the financial crisis and subsequent recession, the Brent-Dubai spread tightened to virtually zero in 2009-10, prompting a 500-600 kbpd year-over-year (yoy) jump in WAF imports to China.

children.title: Crude Imports
children.summary: Crude Runs The Chinese have committed to building 500 MB of strategic petroleum reserve (SPR) capacity by 2016, having completed Phase I of 103 MB in April 2009, and are currently filling the 169 MB of Phase II storage, due to be completed by 2013. A consistent pace of storage filling would suggest and incremental 150-175 kbpd of crude imports to reach 272 MB in 2013, while maintaining 25- 30 days of crude inventories for constantly increasing Chinese refining capacity would imply another 50-75 kbpd of extra crude imports for commercial storage.

children.title: China Share of VLCC Demand
children.summary: This trend in the Chinese share of VLCC demand should continue, as Chinese refiners lift an additional 1.1 mbpd of AG crudes, 0.4 mbpd of Latin American grades and 0.8 mbpd of WAF cargoes during 2011-16. In fact, this forecast pattern of Chinese imports would imply that VLCCs capture 83% of incremental Chinese tonne-mile demand during the period.
